items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: Fletcher invited me in to the band to replace Don.

ctx.x: And did you ever go on the road with Horace Henderson and the Collegians?
Oh yes, yes. We went on the road. And then finally, we were getting some arrangements from Fletcher, his brother, Fletcher Henderson -- and then I
think that Fletcher arranged an engagement for the band in a place called the Club Bamville. I think, which was at 129th Street and Lenox Avenue at the time.

items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Fletcher asked me if I could come and work in . . . substitute for Don Redmond while he was gone

ctx.x: We’ll, of course, discuss Fletcher Henderson, who you had a couple of stints with earlier, I think.

Actually, I think I had had one. I was playing with Billy Fowler’s Orchestra at a club downtown. If I remember correctly, Donald Redmond’s father died, and he had to go back to Piedmont, West Virginia, or Virginia, wherever Piedmont is, and Fletcher asked me if I could come and work in . . . substitute for Don Redmond while he was gone. So I think I asked Billy Fowler, or maybe Fletcher approached him directly, I’m not sure. But Billy said sure, it was okay. He allowed me to do it. And because it was really…
